question: Should OpenClaw standardize this generic ordered configuration-authority model as the core contract for deployment-owned and user-owned settings?
rationale: The RFC intentionally adds core configuration authority, mutation, provenance, and atomic-publication semantics; choosing that architecture over existing read-only includes or a narrower host seam requires maintainer intent.

options.title: Continue generic RFC
options.body: Keep the draft open and review the complete generic authority contract with live mutation and upgrade proof.

options.title: Narrow to host seam
options.body: Reduce the proposal to the smallest deployment-owned configuration boundary needed by Lobster while preserving ordinary configuration behavior.

options.title: Keep external overlays
options.body: Decline a core authority model and retain deployment-level overlays until a narrower shared requirement is demonstrated.

recommendation.title: Continue generic RFC
recommendation.body: Keep the draft open and review the complete generic authority contract with live mutation and upgrade proof.
